History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
35-year-old male with 3–6 month history of poor appetite, low energy/mood, episodic palpitations/subjective dyspnoea in lifts, 1-stone weight loss, and intermittent nausea. Past history of untreated hypothyroidism. Clinician arranged baseline blood investigations and safety-netting advice.

History:
• Presenting complaints  
  – Reduced appetite, low energy, feeling “down” for ≈3.5 months (since starting new law firm).  
  – Weight loss ≈1 stone over ≈6 months.  
  – Episodic palpitations and sense of breathlessness primarily when in a lift; no limitation when walking ≈1 mile.  
  – Intermittent nausea; no vomiting.  
  – Occasional headaches at work.  
  – Wife reports ↓ libido / performance (“nightly activities”).  

• Associated & review of systems  
  – Gastrointestinal: Normal bowel motions; no diarrhoea, blood, or mucus. No acid reflux.  
  – Respiratory: No cough.  
  – Cardiovascular: Palpitations during episodes; no chest pain.  
  – Constitutional: Weight loss, fatigue, low mood.  
  – ENT/Neuro: No data.  
  – Genitourinary: Sexual performance issues (qualitative).  
  – Endocrine: History of hypothyroidism; off replacement.  

• Exacerbating/relieving factors  
  – Palpitations/shortness of breath triggered by being in a lift; not by walking.  
  – No specific food triggers for nausea.  

Past Medical History:
• Hypothyroidism (previously on thyroxine; stopped after changing doctor; last blood test “a long time ago”).  
  – Medication: Levothyroxine – dose/route/frequency not documented – currently not taking.

Social History:
• Occupation: Lawyer (recent job change 3.5 months ago).  
• Marital status: Married.  
• Exercise: Not walking/exercising recently due to poor energy.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs: Not documented.  

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• No examination performed; no vitals recorded.

Investigations:
• Planned: “General set of bloods” – CBC, renal profile, liver function, thyroid panel, vitamin levels, others per GP protocol (not yet performed).

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Constitutional symptoms (fatigue, weight loss, anorexia)  
  – Differential includes anaemia, thyroid dysfunction (possibly uncontrolled hypothyroidism vs hyperthyroidism), depression, systemic illness.  
  – Plan: Order baseline bloods (CBC, U&E, LFT, TFTs, vitamin B12/folate, ferritin). Review results and reassess.

Issue 2: Palpitations/episodic dyspnoea  
  – Currently infrequent, exertional capacity preserved, no chest pain.  
  – Plan: Monitor symptoms; patient advised to present to ED if chest pain, persistent palpitations, or worsening dyspnoea occur. Further work-up (ECG, physical exam) after blood results or sooner if symptoms escalate.

Issue 3: Inactive hypothyroidism (off thyroxine)  
  – Plan: Check thyroid function tests. Reinstitute/adjust levothyroxine depending on results.

General plan items:  
• Safety-net: Return/ED for chest pain, significant bowel change, vomiting, or clinical deterioration.  
• Coordination: Patient to phone support number via app to arrange phlebotomy; GP will issue lab form and text when results returned.  
• Follow-up: Book follow-up appointment once blood results available.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing but expected: Allergies, full medication list, family history, vitals, physical exam findings, smoking/alcohol history.  
• Internal conflicts: None identified.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; occasional overlap/inaudible phrases but overall understandable.
